book.title: Scrum: The Art of Doing Twice the Work in Half the Time
book.author: Jeff Sutherland and J.J. Sutherland

confidence_note: Mechanics from Wikipedia (under 15 minutes, same time and place, progress and obstacles, no detailed discussion); the three questions from standard Scrum, not re-read in the book. Old text's three named effects and 'hundreds of coordination needs' dropped. No case, so a mechanism story at the low end.
facts: The daily scrum lasts under 15 minutes.
It happens at the same time and place every day.
Its purpose is to announce progress toward the sprint goal and any obstacles hindering it, without detailed discussion.
The three questions: what did you do yesterday, what will you do today, what is in your way.
A sprint is usually one to four weeks, most often two.
Each sprint ends with a demonstration of working increments to stakeholders and a retrospective with one or two improvements.
tension: A meeting meant to be shorter than most coffee breaks is meant to catch problems before they grow.
opening_idea: Open on the time limit and the three questions.

lessons.idea: Say the obstacle out loud when it appears and take the discussion elsewhere
lessons.anchor: stand-up under 15 minutes with progress and obstacles; Everyday: a plumber who tells the shop on Monday morning that one part is missing, so someone orders it that day

reflect_final: What obstacle are you carrying right now that nobody on your team knows about yet?

use_cases.situation: The team's weekly meeting drags on
use_cases.move: Scrum keeps the daily meeting under fifteen minutes, three questions only. Can we try that for a week and take details offline?

use_cases.situation: A teammate has gone quiet on a task
use_cases.move: What is in your way today? I just want to know if I can help.
Each morning I will write: done yesterday, doing today, what is in my way. Two minutes.

pocket_idea: Under fifteen minutes, same place, three questions: say what is in your way early, then go back to work.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Scrum's daily meeting is capped at fifteen minutes and its job is to name what is blocking the work.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: The daily scrum is short on purpose: under fifteen minutes, at the same time and place each day. Everyone says what they did yesterday, what they will do today and what is in their way. Details wait for later. The point is to name obstacles early, while there is time to fix them.
